questions.questionText:
[READING PASSAGE FOR QUESTIONS NO. 1 - 3] Evaluating Digital Information in the Modern Age: In today's interconnected world, discerning credible information from misinformation has become an indispensable life skill. Not every article published on social media or search engines can be trusted as factual. When conducting research or reading online news, critical thinkers must look for specific indicators of validity. A reliable source typically provides a verifiable author with relevant credentials, clearly lists the exact date of publication or latest update, cites empirical data or trusted references, and presents content with an objective tone rather than emotionally charged sensationalism.

Choose two signs of a reliable source of information based on the text.
questions.optionA: There is a certain date of the event.
questions.optionB: There is an explicit place of the event.
questions.optionC: There is a clear source of information.
questions.optionD: There is a specific description of the event.

Not every article published on social media or search engines can be trusted as factual. When conducting research or reading online news, critical thinkers must look for specific indicators of validity. A reliable source typically provides a verifiable author with relevant credentials, clearly lists the exact date of publication or latest update, cites empirical data or trusted references, and presents content with an objective tone rather than emotionally charged sensationalism.

What should we do first after we read information online that makes us emotional? Choose one correct answer.
questions.optionA: Check if the source is relevant to the story. A health issue should be discussed by doctors, not politicians.
questions.optionB: Recognize if there is a time for the event. Something that happens not in the present time could be a hoax.
questions.optionC: Read further if there is a detailed description of the event. Nothing should be hidden from public eyes or else they are hoaxes.
questions.optionD: Find out if other sources also cover the story. When all TVs also discuss that, somebody must have paid a lot of money to do it.

questions.questionText:
[READING PASSAGE FOR QUESTIONS NO. 4 - 6] Life in the Boarding School Dormitory: Living in an Islamic boarding school (madrasah asrama) requires students to adhere to a structured daily routine. Every student is assigned a specific schedule for waking up before dawn, performing congregational prayers, memorizing verses of the holy Quran, and maintaining cleanliness in their shared rooms. Once in a while, some students bring homemade delicacies prepared by their families to share with their dorm mates, fostering a strong sense of brotherhood and empathy that lasts well beyond their academic years.

Choose two correct answers based on the text. Why does the writer once in a while bring the food to school?
questions.optionA: It is high time for her to go to school.
questions.optionB: She wants to have her second breakfast.
questions.optionC: There is no more time to have breakfast.
questions.optionD: She wants to have breakfast with friends.
